transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-01
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Rachel Kim (Redwood AE), Marco Silva (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Daniel Park (Sapphire Procurement), Anita Rao (Sapphire Legal), Samir Malik (Sapphire CTO), Leah Ortiz (Sapphire Security)

Auto-generated Summary:
- Procurement/Legal kickoff to align on MSA/DPA, SLAs, pricing approvals and next steps for vendor onboarding.
- High-level technical pilot and security requirements discussed (VPC, KMS, SOC2 evidence).
- Action items: Redwood to share final redlines/pricing; customer to share KMS and compliance checklist; schedule pilot.

Transcript:
[00:00] Rachel Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll give a quick agenda, go over MSA/DPA redlines, SLA ask, and then Marco will cover technical pilot scope.
[00:12] Daniel Park: Yep sounds good, thanks. We have Anita from legal and Leah from security on the line.
[00:18] Anita Rao: hi, thanks.
[00:20] Marco Silva: Hi all, Marco here, i'll try to keep the tech bits concise — focusing on deployment modes — hosted vs dedicated vs private vpc.
[00:30] Samir Malik: quick note, our big trigger is: data residency + KMS integration. We need to know if Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for keys and whether logs can be routed to our SIEM.
[00:45] Priya Nair: absolutely — we do support KMS integrations in our Private offering, and audit logs can be exported. we'll share the specific connectors.
[01:05] Anita Rao: On the DPA, we've got two substantive asks: 1) retention windows and guaranteed deletion; 2) subprocessor list and notification timeline. Are those in the standard DPA?
[01:20] Rachel Kim: standard DPA includes retention and deletion language, yes. we can provide a subprocessor list and we typically give a 30-day notice for new subprocessors. if you need a different notice window we can discuss.
[01:35] Anita Rao: we'd prefer 14 days for high-risk subprocessors, is that something you can accept or we need to escalate?
[01:42] Rachel Kim: i can take that back to legal — usually 30 days is the baseline but 14 for high-risk is not unheard of. i'll flag as an item.
[02:05] Leah Ortiz: on encryption, we also need to confirm both in-transit and at-rest AES-256 and customer KMS control. also, who has access to telemetry logs inside Redwood?
[02:20] Marco Silva: telemetry's access is role-based; we can provide SOC 2 evidence showing RBAC and restricted access. for runtime encryption we support TLS and AES-256 at rest. for customer-managed keys, Private can be configured with your KMS.
[02:40] Samir Malik: okay good. another question on SLA — our procurement requires a 99.9% uptime SLA and a formal credit structure tied to availability. what's Redwood's typical SLA for Dedicated versus Hosted?
[02:55] Rachel Kim: Dedicated typically comes with 99.95% or 99.9% depending on contract tier. Hosted is generally best-effort for standard customers but we can escalate with an enterprise SLA. we can share the SLA matrix in the pack.
[03:15] Daniel Park: pricing approval loop: we need pricing sheet and a clear cost model for tokens and dedicated commit. can you provide an example monthly commit for our expected volume?
[03:30] Rachel Kim: yes we'll send a pricing workbook. just to align, what volumes are you projecting?
[03:35] Daniel Park: initial pilot ~10M tokens/month, ramp to 80–100M over 6 months if things go well.
[03:45] Rachel Kim: ok we have committed plans that map to those volumes — i'll include dedicated capacity options and a cost per 1M token breakdown plus embedding pricing.
[03:58] Anita Rao: on indemnity and liability caps — our legal team usually requests mutual indemnities and a liability cap tied to fees. are you open to a split liability cap?
[04:12] Rachel Kim: Redwood legal prefers a fees-based cap but we can negotiate. i'll mark it as a redline item and propose language if you'd like.
[04:25] Anita Rao: please do. also need to confirm data residency clause — we must ensure EU data stays in EU regions for our EU customers.
[04:35] Marco Silva: region pinning is possible; we can route requests to EU-hosted clusters for your EU tenants. there might be slight latency differences but it's doable.
[04:50] Leah Ortiz: one small thing — do you have an audit or attestation beyond SOC2? ISO 27001?
[04:58] Priya Nair: we have SOC2 Type II and are in process for ISO 27001. we'll share the latest attestation and the security pack.
[05:10] Samir Malik: for the pilot, we'd like a throughput test: 50 concurrent streams and 4k seq length — want to confirm Redwood Dedicated can handle sustained throughput without significant latency spikes.
[05:28] Marco Silva: yes that test is reasonable. we'll run through our Dedicated config — GPU pool sizing, batching, KV-cache behavior. note: if you use prefix caching and steady-state batching, cost per token can drop substantially.
[05:45] Daniel Park: Marco, can you run an initial perf test against an open model and share the spreadsheet metrics (p99 latency, p50, throughput)?
[05:55] Marco Silva: yep, i'll do p50/p95/p99 and throughput, and include memory usage and KV cache hit rate. i'll also include a note on quantization profiles we used — sometimes the numbers change if we switch int8 vs fp16.
[06:20] Anita Rao: re: subprocessors — please include your infra partners, e.g. cloud providers. we've seen 'Redwood Dedicated' vendor docs reference AWS, GCP, and Azure — is that correct?
[06:32] Rachel Kim: right now we have multi-cloud partners typical across AWS/GCP/Azure; Dedicated can be in customers' cloud or our dedicated pools depending on contract.
[06:45] Daniel Park: procurement approvals: what docs do we need to route to finance for sign-off? typically MSA, DPA, pricing, SLA matrix, and a security pack.
[06:58] Rachel Kim: that's our standard bundle — we'll drop a zipped pack with the legal redlines, security attestation, and pricing workbook.
[07:10] Leah Ortiz: for KMS keys, we need confirmation on key rotation policies and whether Redwood requires access to the plain text keys at any point.
[07:20] Marco Silva: you keep keys in your KMS — Redwood never has the plaintext keys. we integrate using standard envelope encryption. rotation policies you manage; we'll document integration steps.
[07:42] Anita Rao: please add a clause that Redwood will not reuse customer data for model training — it must be explicit in the DPA.
[07:50] Rachel Kim: yes that's in our DPA for enterprise customers; we'll ensure the language is explicit about no training access without opt-in.
[08:05] Daniel Park: timeline question — we want a 30–60 day window to get procurement signed and start the pilot. is that realistic?
[08:15] Rachel Kim: yes, if we get the redlines quickly we can aim for a 30-day procurement cycle. pilot could start within 1–2 weeks after contract is signed.
[08:30] Priya Nair: i'll coordinate onboarding and a pilot schedule; Marco will lead the perf runs and i'll handle success criteria tracking.
[08:45] Marco Silva: for success criteria, what are your SLOs? latency under 300ms p95 for chat use, and throughput of 5k tokens/s sustained?
[08:58] Samir Malik: p95 300ms is tight, but for low-context calls maybe. we'll start with p95 < 500ms for the pilot and aim to optimize.
[09:10] Rachel Kim: understood, we'll note pilot SLOs as p95 < 500ms and target improvements.
[09:22] Anita Rao: also need to confirm indemnity around data breaches and notification timelines — 72 hours standard?
[09:30] Rachel Kim: yes we typically commit to timely notification — 72 hours is standard for serious incidents; we'll provide exact contractual language in the MSA.
[09:45] Daniel Park: any known blockers on Redwood side for onboarding large enterprise — e.g., procurement terms you don't accept?
[09:55] Rachel Kim: usual negotiation areas are liability caps, data residency specifics and subprocessor notice windows; those are negotiable but need to be highlighted early.
[10:10] Leah Ortiz: technical question: will logs include prompt text? we need to ensure prompt text isn't included in logs by default to protect PII.
[10:20] Marco Silva: by default telemetry is anonymized; prompt text is not stored in application logs unless you opt into it for debugging. we'll document how to turn on/off full-text logging.
[10:38] Anita Rao: good. final note: please provide an editable MSA/DPA with redlines so our counsel can mark up.
[10:45] Rachel Kim: i'll send the editable docs. Anita, expect to see a tracked-change MSA and DPA by Thursday 2027-03-04.
[10:55] Daniel Park: great. thank you.
[11:00] Marco Silva: i'll kick off the perf test after we get a test account and sample workload — want to share a workload spec?
[11:10] Samir Malik: yes we'll share a synthetic workload and production-like prompt set by EOD tomorrow.
[11:18] Priya Nair: i'll schedule the pilot kickoff meeting once we have signed contract dates — proposed week of 2027-03-14.
[11:28] Rachel Kim: recap of next steps: 1) Rachel sends MSA/DPA redlines + pricing sheet by 2027-03-04; 2) Anita shares KMS/policy checklist by 2027-03-07; 3) Marco runs perf tests and shares results w/ spreadsheet by 2027-03-18; 4) Priya schedules pilot week of 2027-03-14.
[11:50] Daniel Park: that works, thanks everyone.
[12:00] Anita Rao: thanks.
[12:05] Leah Ortiz: bye.

End of transcript.
